source_text: Ac per hoc inconcussa manet nostra responsio, quae ostendit per unum hominem non generatione vitiatam atque corruptam, sed integra permanente natura vitiosam solummodo allegari ab Apostolo peccantium voluntatem.
pass_a_gloss: And through this our response remains unshaken, which shows that through one human not a generation vitiated and corrupted, but with nature remaining intact only the vicious will of those sinning is alleged by the Apostle.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Consequently, our answer remains unshaken. It shows that the apostle does not claim that generation was damaged and corrupted through one man. Rather, nature remains intact, and only the will of sinners is shown to be corrupt.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Repeats or discusses sin entering or passing through one man.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
